scenes.title: Follow one input to its output
The inputs are already in GPU memory
The CPU prints the copied results

cues.text: The starter doubles five input values.
Follow input[2] to output[2]. How does the thread choose that position?
The supplied setup already copies the inputs into GPU memory.
Leave that setup unchanged for this experiment.
We follow block zero’s local thread two.
Zero times four, plus two, gives array index two.
The same index selects input[2] and output[2].
An SM, or streaming multiprocessor, is execution hardware on the GPU chip.
It runs the selected thread’s instructions.
The thread reads 3.0 from input[2] in GPU memory.
That value becomes working state for its instructions on the SM.
The SM’s arithmetic hardware multiplies 3.0 by 2.0, producing 6.0.
Threads keep their own working values while sharing this hardware.
The thread writes 6.0 to output[2] in GPU memory.
Its index fixes the destination even if other threads finish first.
main copies the GPU results into CPU memory and prints Output.
Return to the lesson. Find runKernel in the CUDA source editor.
Change its multiplier from 2.0f to 4.0f.
Pause. Predict the third Output value and the hardware doing the multiply.
Click Compile and run. Return to this recording to compare your result.
With 4.0f, input[2] still supplies 3.0 and output[2] becomes 12.0.
The same index chooses the destination; the SM still performs the multiply.
The index selects data. The SM performs arithmetic. GPU memory holds the arrays.
Lesson three explores the launch size.
